note: Frozen evaluation set B. A SECOND frozen set, added because power on set A is capped by the PROMPT count, not the sample count (see docs/measurements/behaviour-tt-tnt-v1-vs-v3.md, 'Power, and why more samples will not help much'). Set A (docs/evaluation_prompts.json) is untouched and stays the cross-checkpoint reference. These are NEVER pooled with set A's prompts into one score: two sets written at different times by different means are not exchangeable, and averaging them would quietly redefine the metric. Report B beside A, never inside it. Do not edit prompts between runs -- that breaks comparability. Add new ones with new ids instead.
design: Ids are all prefixed 'b-' so no id can collide with set A's (voice-, stutter-, oracle-, agentic-, ground-, assoc-, long-).

Two orthogonal axes. The id prefix after 'b-' names the CORPUS REGISTER the opening leans toward, using train/corpus.py's source names; the 'probe' field names the BEHAVIOUR the prompt stresses, using set A's probe vocabulary plus one new tag.

Prompts were derived from the corpus design -- train/corpus.py's per-source rationales and docs/corpus_blend.md -- and NOT from any model's observed output. No prompt here was chosen because some checkpoint failed on something like it. An instrument reverse-engineered from the last bug cannot find the next one.
Registers (45): spine 6, procedural 7, weird 4, folklore 4, gutenberg_children 3, wikipedia_simple 4, poetry 2, flavour 5, tinystories 2, neutral 8.
Probes (45): target-voice 7, agentic 7, coherence 7, grounding 5, perpendicular 5, oracular 3, stutter 3, default-register 8.

procedural gets the largest register block after the neutral one because it is the slice that measurably benefits most from long context (+0.130 at 3x SEM in docs/measurements/context-use-tt-tnt-v3.md), so it is where a context-window change should show first.

'default-register' (b-null-*) is a new probe tag with no set A analogue: eight openings that lean toward NO slice -- no imperative, no archaism, no apparatus, no definition frame, no fairy-tale noun -- so the model's DEFAULT register is measurable and not only its steerability. Set A can only see what the model does when a register is handed to it. These are slice-NEUTRAL, not register-free in any absolute sense; that is not achievable in English, and claiming it would be dishonest.

The two tinystories-register prompts (b-tiny-*) are reachability controls, not bait. 31% of the blend is that register; a set in which the backbone register is unreachable on every prompt would leave the story-frame signal at the floor for every model, which is the state in which no comparison can resolve anything.

Termination needs both kinds of prompt to be measurable. b-spine-06, b-proc-06, b-folk-03 and b-tiny-02 sit close to a natural close, so a model that has learned </s> has somewhere to put it; the rest open a continuation.

Deviations from a straight 3x scaling of set A's probe mix, stated rather than hidden: agentic is up (long-context rationale above); oracular and stutter are down, because flavour is 0.5% of the blend and stutter prompts are excluded from one of the two repetition aggregates anyway, so they buy less per prompt.
